latest_wiki.summary: In August 1919 the Soviet government seized Jewish properties, including synagogues, and many Jewish communities were dissolved.
The Doctors' plot culminated in a show trial of a group of doctors, almost all of whom were Jewish, for supposedly plotting to assassinate Stalin.
By 1947-48, Jews in German universities in the Soviet Occupation Zone who resisted Sovietisation were characterized as having a 'non-Aryan background'.
Within a week after the 1967 Six-Day War, Jewish radio engineer Boris Kochubievsky was called to the KGB bureau and taken without questioning to a mental institution in Kiev.
During the anti-cosmopolitan campaign after 1948, numerous Yiddish-writing poets, writers, painters and sculptors were arrested or killed.
The text reports that pogroms against Jews continued during 1918-1920, carried out by both the Red and White armies.
In the show trial of the 'Trotskyite-Zinovievite Terrorist Center', Bolshevik leaders were accused of hiding their Jewish origins under Slavic names.
Richard Baumhammers fired into the windows of the Beth El Congregation synagogue and spray-painted two red swastikas on the building.
Two classroom windows at Temple Israel in Alameda were smashed.
A lone gunman opened fire at the El Al airline ticket counter at Los Angeles International Airport. Two people were killed and four injured before the gunman was shot by a security guard.
The text reports an antisemitic attack in Berlin, Germany on 17 April 2018.
The Students for Justice in Palestine chapter at UC Irvine was sanctioned for disrupting a program hosted by a Jewish campus group in May. The text says it also intimidated Jewish students.

latest_jta.summary: Trofimov murdered the Jewish worker Bolsheminikov in a Soviet factory in Pskov, and his trial opened in Pskov. A local paper reported that a few days later an anti-Semitic incident occurred and that the local Communist official refused to arrest the offender.

Peasants in the village of Pluk spread a rumor that a Jewish farmer had sold a Christian farmhand for ritual purposes, and a public meeting was held on the accusation. The farmhand's return ended the accusation, and the Jewish farmer began libel proceedings against his accusers.
The article reports that Malishev, a member of the town Soviet, said at a session on anti-Semitism that the Jews rather than anti-Semitism should be fought, and the Soviet denounced him.
A deputy asked the Romanian Minister of the Interior to act against anti-Semitic excesses in Briceni. The Jewish paper Adeverul says a detailed account confirms the outrages were barbaric.

After a street collision in which a Christian servant girl was cut, a crowd spread a ritual murder rumor against a Jewish barber, Hillel Nigus, and attempted to lynch him. The mob broke the windows and doors of the restaurant where he had taken refuge, and police later dispersed the crowd.

According to the Bundist paper Volkszeitung, Communists attacked Jewish needle workers of the Right Wing in Poland. Shops were invaded and workers were attacked with knives, shears and hammers, and many were injured.

Troops were sent to Deliatyn in Galicia after a continued anti-Jewish agitation, and peasants from neighboring villages joined an anti-Jewish demonstration in the town. A guard of Zionist youths was placed around Jewish barracks because of fear of arson.
The article reports that two brothers, Lavrentiev, were sentenced to two years' imprisonment each for spreading anti-Semitic propaganda at a factory in Borovitchi.

The article reports that a Communist worker, Trofimov, was sentenced by a Pskov court to five years' imprisonment for murdering his Jewish fellow worker, Bolsheminikov, and that the defense said he was an anti-Semite.

During Purim celebrations, villagers attacked Jewish homes at Bialoczow after a rumor that Purim players had profaned a cross. Windows in seventeen Jewish homes were smashed, according to the Ministry of the Interior.

Representative Isidore H. Fox told a legislative committee that the Boston School Committee avoided appointing a Jewish attendance officer despite a qualified Jewish candidate. He charged that the committee manipulated its votes to block a Jewish appointment.

According to the paper Lupta, anti-Semitic hooligans at Clausenburg attacked Jewish passersby and seriously injured three Jewish citizens. The paper says the culprits were known to the authorities but went unpunished.

A 19-year-old employee of the Vologda Sanitation Department attempted to organize a society under the slogan 'Kill the Jews, Save Russia' and wrote a secret circular for it. He was sentenced to three months' imprisonment after an investigation.

Under an edict issued in Yemen, police searched for Jewish orphans and tried to force them to convert to Islam. Children who refused were beaten and imprisoned in cellars, according to a letter published in Doar Ha'yom.

latest_research.summary: The Observatory on Antisemitism in Belgium reports that a paving stone was thrown through a third-floor window of the Orthodox Jewish community synagogue in Anderlecht, shattering the glass. The Observatory describes it as vandalism targeting a Jewish place of worship, and the US ambassador calls it an antisemitic attack. The perpetrator is unidentified.

Jewish News reports that a woman was filmed describing Jewish people as "killers and psychopaths" during a protest outside Sheffield Town Hall. South Yorkshire Police first recorded a hate incident. A later Jewish News report says police concluded the remarks did not amount to a recordable crime, and the lower, no-crime finding is the one noted here.

Two unknown persons threw Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel synagogue complex on Brunnenstraße in Berlin-Mitte in the early morning. According to reports the devices landed on the pavement and no one was hurt.

A 26-year-old Jewish student wearing a kippah was struck on the head with a folding spade outside the Hohe Weide synagogue, according to the sources. Police assumed an antisemitic motive, and a later court ruling is reported to have found a targeted attack on a Jew.

Unknown persons scratched swastikas into several gravestones at the Jewish cemetery on Krankenhausstraße in Cloppenburg, and state security police investigated for incitement to hatred. Police later reported that two teenagers admitted the act.
Witnesses told police that a group of about 15 people gathered in front of the synagogue, shouted and burned an Israeli flag. State security police took over the investigation.

Police reported that a 24-year-old Jewish man was assaulted on a tram in Erfurt after another man noticed his Star of David necklace. The attacker tried to drag him off the tram, kicked him and later threatened him, and is being investigated for a politically motivated hate crime.

Berlin police reported that an unidentified man punched a 60-year-old man to the ground in a park after learning that he was Jewish, and the victim had minor facial injuries. State security police are investigating suspected aggravated assault with an antisemitic motive.
Unknown persons damaged the glass of the synagogue entrance door with stones, and police found a partly burned Israeli flag in front of it, according to the reports. Three suspects were arrested.

About 180 people moved from the station forecourt toward the synagogue in an unregistered rally, and antisemitic chants were shouted, according to a press report. Church bodies described the events near the synagogue as antisemitic riots.

RIAS reports that a resident of an asylum shelter in Coburg attacked another resident with a knife because he took him for a Jew. The Coburg prosecutor's office is reported to have assumed the perpetrator was not criminally responsible.

The entrance door of a residential house in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg was sprayed with a Star of David. State security police investigated on suspicion of incitement to hatred (Volksverhetzung), and the press reported that the marking apparently aimed to intimidate Jewish residents.
